evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/api.ts:253 — the response interceptor's 401 branch does `const rotatedToken = await onUnauthorizedCallback();` with NO try/catch around it. The UnauthorizedHandler contract documented on the same file (lines 54-58) explicitly states: 'Returning null/undefined (or throwing) means the session could not be recovered — the interceptor then rejects the original request and the handler is responsible for any session teardown.' For the null/undefined case the code correctly falls through to `return Promise.reject(transformError(error))` at :304, so consumers get a typed ApiError. For the THROW case the code does not honour the contract: the thrown value escapes the async error handler directly, so (a) it bypasses transformError() and raw getApiClient() consumers receive an untyped rejection instead of an ApiError (breaking isApiError()/getErrorMessage() call sites), and (b) the method/transient retry path at :276-301 is skipped entirely.

Reachability: latent today. The only wired handler is AuthContext.handleUnauthorized (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:657-669), which catches refreshToken() rejections internally and awaits logout(), so it currently resolves rather than throws. The gap is a contract-vs-implementation mismatch that will silently misbehave the moment any future onUnauthorized handler (or a synchronous throw inside the current one, e.g. if queryClient.removeQueries threw) rejects. Landable frontend-only remedy confined to api.ts: wrap the await in try/catch and, on throw, fall through to the same `Promise.reject(transformError(error))` path the null branch uses. Confidence medium: the propagation is confirmed by static read of the interceptor; whether a handler ever throws is deployment-dependent, so the trigger is latent rather than runtime-confirmed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:83-95 — the single-subscription effect guards with `if (!eventType || !handlerRef.current) return;` and has dependency list `[eventType, subscribe]`. `handler` is deliberately kept out of the deps (stored in handlerRef at :79-80 to avoid re-subscribing on handler identity churn). The failure mode: if a caller passes `useWebSocket(eventType, handler)` where `handler` is undefined on the render that first supplies a non-null `eventType` (e.g. `useWebSocket('notification.created', ready ? onEvent : undefined)`), the effect runs, hits the early-return because handlerRef.current is undefined, and creates NO subscription. When `handler` later becomes defined WITHOUT eventType or subscribe changing, the effect does not re-run (handler is not a dep and not surfaced via any other dep), so the subscription is never established — events for that eventType are silently dropped for the component's lifetime.

Contrast: the sibling useWebSocketSubscriptions (:142-159) keys its effect on eventTypesKey and reads handlers from subscriptionsRef, so a handler swap for an existing key is safe there; but useWebSocket has no equivalent re-arm when the handler transitions undefined->defined. Reachability: latent — most call sites pass a stable defined handler at mount, so it rarely bites. Landable frontend-only remedy confined to useWebSocket.ts: either subscribe unconditionally (the wrappedHandler already no-ops via `handlerRef.current?.(message)` when undefined) so the subscription exists regardless of initial handler presence, or add a boolean `hasHandler` derived value to the dependency list so the effect re-runs when the handler first appears. Verifiable with a Vitest render that starts handler=undefined then rerenders with a defined handler and asserts subscribe() was called. Confidence medium: the missed re-subscribe is confirmed by static read of the deps; triggering requires the initially-undefined-handler usage pattern, so it is latent.
